column3: NASB follows the critical text (“beloved”); “servant” is rendered “bond-servant,” and “in Jesus Christ” “for Jesus Christ.”
“Would be multiplied” is rendered “May … be multiplied.”
NASB follows the critical text (“our common salvation”); “exhorting” is rendered “appealing.”
NASB follows the critical text (“our only Master and Lord,” without “God”); “stealthily” is rendered “unnoticed,” and “sensuality” “licentiousness.”
NASB follows the critical text (“all things once for all”); it reads “the Lord.”
“Dwelling” is rendered “abode,” and “chains” “bonds.”
“Set forth” is rendered “exhibited,” and NASB adds “gross.”
“Glorious ones” is rendered “angelic majesties.”
“A judgment of blasphemy” is rendered “a railing judgment.”
“Corrupt themselves” is rendered “are destroyed,” and NASB moves “like unreasoning animals.”
“For reward” is rendered “for pay”; NASB uses perfect tenses.
NASB follows the critical text (“carried along”); “twice having died” is rendered “doubly dead,” and “shepherding themselves” “caring for themselves.”
“Foaming out” is rendered “casting up … like foam,” and “gloom of darkness” “black darkness.”
“Seventh from Adam” is rendered “in the seventh generation from Adam,” and “myriads” “many thousands.”
NASB reads “all the ungodly,” which matches the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “every soul.” NASB restructures the clause.
“Discontented” is rendered “finding fault”; “speaks great swelling words” is rendered “speak arrogantly.”
“Declarations” is rendered “words”; NASB supplies “ought to.”
NASB follows the critical text (“In the last time”); “scoffers” is rendered “mockers.”
“Not having the Spirit” is rendered “devoid of the Spirit.”
“In” is rendered “on.”
“Awaiting” is rendered “waiting anxiously for.”
NASB follows the critical text (three groups); “those who are doubting” is rendered “some, who are doubting.”
NASB follows the critical text (“on some have mercy with fear”); “stained” is rendered “polluted.”
NASB follows the critical text (“you”); “exultation” is rendered “great joy.”
NASB follows the critical text (“through Jesus Christ our Lord,” “before all time,” without “wise”).
